note: Every item here (Nikkei order cuts, memory costs, unit trackers, Duo shortage) is wire-level preview copy on a $3.5T name whose median print reaction is ~0.9%; the only genuinely unpriced variable is the level of the December GM/revenue guide, so the whole set is sized to fractions of a point with a mild negative tilt against an 86th-percentile put skew and a record run-up.

Item 0 is the kind LESSONS says pays: arithmetic across three separate company releases (the 2026-07-14 8-K's $100.6M effective backlog, the $22M Aug AI burn-in order, the ~$6M Oct Sonoma follow-on) showing disclosed orders already cover the low end of the $130-150M FY27 guide, which no preview adds up and which lands on the exact line the last three prints were bought on (+21.9/+25.7/+16.0); item 2's 18.05% float short at 2.0 days to cover into a 49% drawdown is a squeeze mechanism in its own right, netted against the Teradyne digestion read (item 5) and the component-cost margin risk (item 3).

Item 1 carries it: the FY guide less Q1/Q2 and a Q3 printing $237-245M on the four-quarter beat habit implies a roughly flat-to-down Q4 of ~$239M, which is the same setup that produced -15.06% in Nov 2025 — but the hunter's own independence text concedes that reaction was attributed to a GAAP loss, so this is inference rather than a document, sized below the run-up/skew backdrop it rests on and partly offset by the near-certain revenue beat (item 0) and the first quantified 2027 selling-season read (item 6).

Consensus parked 0.8% above the guide midpoint against +7.6% and +8.8% historical beats (item 0), corroborated by the 10-Q deferred-revenue walk no preview quotes (item 8) and federal obligations past $1bn (item 4), into a tape already 14% off the Oct 9 high (item 1) — but LESSONS 1 is the live risk here and ServiceNow's -15.25% on an in-line print (item 2) is the explicit evidence that the reaction function for a good-but-not-outstanding beat at 61x revenue is harsh, which is why the number is well under the implied move.

The fundamental case is strong and negative — consensus of $365.5M is flat on Q2 while the company's own pre-released originations fell 2.6% q/q, implying ~$355M (item 0), and the reaffirmed FY guide needs an H2 ramp the street has simply copied rather than modelled (item 1) — but it is also the most priced name in the pack: 52-week low, +16.76 skew paying for downside, and 33.4% of float short at 6.4 days to cover with a +31.8% precedent in the right tail (item 4), plus the hunter's own honest counterweight that per-day originations accelerated into September with UMI at the guide assumption (item 2). Near-balanced, mildly negative.
